title: Temples, Khao Soi & Gentle Giants in Chiang Mai
summary: A relaxed three days for four friends: the Old City's Lanna temples, the mountain-top views of Doi Suthep, and a day with rescued elephants. This is the built-in sample — add an API key to plan your own trips.
bestTime: November to February is cool and dry; expect warm afternoons around 30°C and cool mornings in the hills.
gettingAround: Red songthaews (shared trucks) and Grab cover the city; charter a songthaew for Doi Suthep and book tours with hotel pickup for trips out of town.

days.title: Old City temples and Lanna culture

items.name: Wat Phra Singh
items.description: Start at the Old City's most revered temple, home to the Phra Singh Buddha and the gilded Viharn Lai Kham.
items.priceNote: Entry to the Viharn Lai Kham
items.tip: Cover shoulders and knees; sarongs are lent at the gate.

items.name: Wat Chedi Luang
items.description: Wander around the massive 15th-century ruined chedi, once home to the Emerald Buddha.
items.tip: Monk Chat runs most afternoons if you want to ask the monks questions.

items.name: Khao Soi Mae Sai
items.description: Lunch on Chiang Mai's signature curry noodle soup at a much-loved local shop.
items.placeQuery: Khao Soi Mae Sai, Chiang Mai
items.tip: It closes mid-afternoon once the soup runs out.

items.name: Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Centre
items.description: Air-conditioned galleries that tell the story of Lanna history in an elegant colonial building behind the Three Kings Monument.
items.placeQuery: Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Centre
items.wikiTitle: Chiang Mai City Arts and Cultural Centre

items.name: Tha Phae Gate
items.description: Watch the pigeons and the evening light on the restored brick gate; on Sundays the walking street starts here.

items.name: Huen Phen
items.description: Northern Thai dinner of sai oua sausage, nam prik ong and gaeng hang lay in an antique-filled house.

days.title: Doi Suthep views and Nimman cafés

items.name: Songthaew charter to Doi Suthep
items.description: Charter a red truck from the zoo/university stop up the winding mountain road and back.
items.placeQuery: Doi Suthep songthaew stop, Chiang Mai University
items.priceNote: Round trip with waiting time, whole truck
items.tip: Agree the price and the stops before you get in.

items.name: Wat Phra That Doi Suthep
items.description: Climb the 306-step naga staircase to the golden chedi and the view over the whole city.
items.tip: Take the tram up for 20 THB if the stairs are too much.

items.name: Bhubing Palace
items.description: Stroll the royal winter residence's rose gardens and cool pine forest.
items.tip: Closed when the royal family is in residence.

items.name: One Nimman
items.description: Late lunch and coffee in the red-brick courtyard at the heart of Nimman.

items.name: Maya Lifestyle Shopping Center
items.description: Browse Thai design shops and catch the sunset from the rooftop.
items.placeQuery: Maya Lifestyle Shopping Center, Chiang Mai

items.name: Chiang Mai Night Bazaar
items.description: Graze through food stalls and bargain for souvenirs at the city's sprawling night market.
items.tip: Start your bargaining at about half the asking price.

items.name: Elephant Nature Park
items.description: Observe and feed rescued elephants at an ethical sanctuary — no riding, no shows.
items.priceNote: Single-day visit with hotel pickup and lunch
items.tip: Book a few weeks ahead; days sell out in high season.

items.name: Warorot Market
items.description: Pick up dried fruit, nam prik and Lanna textiles at the locals' favourite market.

items.name: Khantoke dinner at Old Chiang Mai Cultural Center
items.description: A traditional Lanna banquet served on low tables with classical dance performances.

extras.name: Boutique hotel in the Old City (2 rooms × 3 nights)
extras.priceNote: Twin rooms with breakfast, per room per night

tips: Carry small notes — songthaew drivers and market stalls rarely have change for 1,000 THB.
Temples ask for covered shoulders and knees; pack a light scarf.
Grab works well in the city but is scarce up on Doi Suthep, so keep your songthaew waiting.
Tap water is not drinkable; refill stations charge 1 THB per litre.
packing: Light scarf or sarong for temples
Light jacket for Doi Suthep mornings
Clothes you don't mind getting muddy at the elephant park
